# Explicit Voxel/Grid Representations
## Overview
Explicit Voxel/Grid Representations optimize scene parameters (density, color, features) stored in discrete 3D grids or hierarchical structures, avoiding the implicit parameterization of [multi-layer perceptrons](#23740-neural-network-for-transfer-function-parameterization.md) (MLPs) used in [Neural Radiance Fields](4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) [G]. This family distinguishes itself by enabling direct optimization of grid values, which significantly reduces training time and memory overhead compared to [implicit methods](#12421-implicit-methods-sdf-based.md), while offering more structured scene representations than point-based methods like [3D Gaussian Splatting](1795-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Radiance-field optimization](44-radiance-field-optimization.md) [G]. All methods in this family represent the scene using discrete 3D voxel grids or hierarchical grid structures to store parameters such as volume density, color, and features [G]. These parameters are optimized directly from input images, bypassing the need for training large [implicit neural networks](#16052-implicit-neural-networks-neural-fields.md) [G]. The forward rendering model evaluates the [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) along camera rays, integrating density and color samples to produce pixel colors [G]. Gradients are propagated back through the [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) operator to update the voxel grid values [G].

## Subtopics

### [Explicit Radiance Fields](806-explicit-radiance-fields.md)
What it is: A method that reconstructs 3D scenes by formulating [volumetric reconstruction](#12558-reconstruction-and-segmentation.md) as a non-linear least-squares problem solved explicitly using a Gauss-Newton solver, avoiding neural networks. What sets it apart: It represents the scene as a discrete voxel grid for the foreground and a hierarchy of environment maps for the background, achieving significantly faster convergence (2-3 orders of magnitude) compared to implicit radiance fields that use MLPs and Adam optimization, while maintaining comparable quality. When to choose it: When fast convergence without neural networks is required. Link: [Explicit Radiance Fields](806-explicit-radiance-fields.md)

### [Direct Voxel Grid Optimization](4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md)
What it is: A method that reconstructs per-scene radiance fields from calibrated images by directly optimizing a dense 3D [voxel grid for volume](#2393-3d-texture-representation-cpu-gpu-indexing.md) density and a feature voxel grid for color. What sets it apart: It eliminates the need for lengthy MLP training compared to implicit methods, and trains the voxel grid directly from scratch unlike earlier explicit voxel methods. It uses a shallow MLP to handle view-dependent appearance, balancing speed and quality compared to methods that optimize colors directly in the grid. When to choose it: When per-scene optimization in under 15 minutes on a single GPU is needed. Link: [Direct Voxel Grid Optimization](4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md)

### [Canonical Radiance Field with Voxel Grid](8920-canonical-radiance-field-with-voxel-grid.md)
What it is: A method that replaces the continuous, coordinate-based MLP of [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) with a discrete, learnable voxel grid to represent a static scene in a canonical time frame. What sets it apart: It explicitly separates density and color features into distinct grids optimized for canonical static representation, differing from other explicit methods by serving as a foundational static representation for dynamic scene warping rather than direct view synthesis optimization. When to choose it: When a static canonical representation is needed for forward warping in dynamic scenes. Link: [Canonical Radiance Field with Voxel Grid](8920-canonical-radiance-field-with-voxel-grid.md)

### [Forward Flow for Novel View Synthesis of Dynamic Scenes](13903-forward-flow-for-novel-view-synthesis-of-dynamic-scenes.md)
What it is: A [dynamic NeRF](#21867-dynamic-nerf.md) method that replaces backward flow deformation with forward flow to warp a canonical radiance field to target time steps. What sets it apart: It maps canonical space to current time, yielding smooth flow norms for the same 3D position along the timeline, avoiding the discontinuity and non-smoothness of backward flow methods. When to choose it: When smooth and continuous motion modeling is required for dynamic scenes. Link: [Forward Flow for Novel View Synthesis of Dynamic Scenes](13903-forward-flow-for-novel-view-synthesis-of-dynamic-scenes.md)

## Background
Explicit [voxel representations](#19656-voxel-representation.md) emerged as a response to the computational bottlenecks of implicit [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) [G]. Early works like [Explicit Radiance Fields](806-explicit-radiance-fields.md) demonstrated that direct optimization of voxel grids could achieve fast convergence for static scenes [G]. [Direct Voxel Grid Optimization](4694-direct-voxel-grid-optimization.md) later popularized the approach by showing that a [dense voxel grid](#1719-voxel-grid-indexing.md) combined with a shallow MLP could match the quality of NeRF while training orders of magnitude faster [G]. These methods are widely used in real-time rendering, dynamic scene reconstruction, and scenarios requiring rapid per-scene optimization [G].
